questions.q: Long-run economic growth is shown by:
options: A rise in the price level

questions.q: On a PPF, short-run growth using spare capacity is shown by:
options: A move from inside the curve towards it
An outward shift of the curve
An inward shift of the curve
questions.why: Capacity is unchanged, and idle resources are used.

questions.q: Match each factor to the type of growth it mainly drives.
questions.why: Spending drives the short run, and capacity drives the long run.

questions.q: How can growth help a government's finances?
options: More tax revenue, with no rise in tax rates
questions.why: Incomes and spending rise, so taxes bring in more.

questions.q: Sustainable growth means growth that can continue without serious problems for the future.
questions.why: The kind of growth matters, as well as the rate.

questions.q: Explain one possible cost of rapid economic growth.

ideas.label: Names a cost, such as inflation, pollution or inequality
Explains why it follows from growth

questions.model: Rapid growth can cause inflation, because demand rises above capacity and firms raise prices. More output can also add to pollution.
questions.why: Name the cost, then say how growth causes it.

tests.answer: More output causes more pollution, which harms third parties.
